name: Prague Castle
blurb: Hilltop castle complex with St Vitus Cathedral and Golden Lane; go early to beat the crowds.

name: Museum of Communism
blurb: Walks through Czech communist history up to the 1989 Velvet Revolution, with propaganda art and everyday objects on display.
priceText: Adults 390 Kč, students with ID 310 Kč, seniors 340 Kč

name: Mucha Museum
blurb: Works of Art Nouveau master Alphonse Mucha, from his famous posters to paintings, in a compact museum in the New Town.
priceText: Adult 300 Kč; children, students and seniors 220 Kč

name: Speculum Alchemiae
blurb: Tiny alchemy museum in a house said to date from 980 AD, in the old Jewish Quarter; quirky, cheap and off the beaten track.

name: Lokál
blurb: Modern take on a Czech beer hall: cheap Pilsner and hearty traditional dishes in a bright, busy room in the Old Town.

name: Kantýna
blurb: Grab a tray and pile on meat cuts and sides at the counters, paying by weight; a lively, market-style lunch or dinner.

name: U Fleků
blurb: Historic brewery restaurant that brews its own dark, sweet beer; a classic old-school Prague beer hall night out.
priceText: U Fleků 13° 99 Kč and spirits around 79 Kč

name: Chateau Rouge
blurb: Three-floor Old Town club with free entry, cheap Staropramen and a steady flow of tourists and pub-crawl groups.

name: Staropramen Brewery Visitor Center
blurb: Tour Prague's best-known brewery, founded in 1869, with English-language tours and a restaurant on the same site.

name: Schönbrunn Palace
blurb: Habsburg summer palace whose state rooms are the main draw; the palace ticket includes an audio guide.
priceText: Palace Ticket with audio guide: adults € 42.00; children from 6 € 30.00

name: Kunsthistorisches Museum
blurb: One of the world's great art museums, with Bruegel and Rubens in a palatial building; open late on Thursdays.
priceText: Adult € 22 online, € 24 at the museum; reduced € 19 online, € 20 on site; under 19 free

name: Stephansdom
blurb: Gothic cathedral at the heart of the Old Town; the paid tour takes in the cathedral and its treasury.

name: Museum Postsparkasse
blurb: Free museum on Otto Wagner's Post Office Savings Bank; the main banking hall is a showpiece Art Nouveau space.

name: Schnitzelwirt Schmidt
blurb: Old-school schnitzel house in Neubau with huge portions; the farmer's platter (Bauernschmaus) is the big, filling choice.

name: Naschmarkt
blurb: Vienna's largest market, with produce stalls, food stalls and an oriental-flavoured buzz; good for lunch or a browse.
when: Shops Mon–Sat 06:00–19:30 (Sat to 18:00); food stalls Mon–Sat 06:00–23:00

name: Bermuda Triangle
blurb: Inner-city nightlife area with cheap drinks that draws a young crowd; a lively base for a night out.

name: Loos American Bar
blurb: Tiny Art Deco bar designed by Adolf Loos in 1908, a time-warp interior with late opening hours.

name: Burgtheater behind-the-scenes tour
blurb: Guided behind-the-scenes tour of the 1888 Burgtheater, one of Europe's top German-language theatres; a cheap look inside.
when: Sep–Jun at 15:00 daily; Fri–Sun tours also in English

name: Wiener Eislaufverein ice rink
blurb: Big outdoor ice rink of about 6,000 m² in the Landstraße district, a winter favourite for a relaxed afternoon on the ice.

name: Fisherman's Bastion
blurb: White neo-Romanesque terraces on Castle Hill with the best panorama over the Danube, Parliament and Chain Bridge.

name: Matthias Church
blurb: Late-Gothic church on Trinity Square with richly coloured roof tiles and a historic interior; church and tower are ticketed.

name: Museum of Fine Arts (Szépművészeti)
blurb: Big collection of non-Hungarian art, from ancient times to European masters, in a neoclassical building in City Park.

name: Vajdahunyad Castle
blurb: Fairy-tale castle in City Park, built as a full-scale model for Hungary's 1896 millennium; free to visit.

name: Fakanál Restaurant
blurb: Traditional Hungarian home cooking at the Central Market Hall: soups, stews and generous mains at low prices.

name: Pozsony tavern
blurb: Cosy, very cheap Hungarian tavern with big portions, a 15-minute walk from Parliament; a budget dinner that fills you up.

name: Szimpla Kert
blurb: Iconic ruin pub in Erzsébetváros: a maze of mismatched rooms, a courtyard and a cinema, with a bohemian, lively crowd.

name: A38
blurb: Former Ukrainian stone-carrier ship turned music club on the Danube, often rated among Budapest's best party venues.

name: Széchenyi Thermal Bath
blurb: Huge thermal bath complex in City Park with indoor and outdoor mineral-water pools; the classic Budapest bath visit.

name: Dagály Spa
blurb: Budget swimming and thermal complex with outdoor pools open year-round and two hot outdoor baths; a cheaper local option.

name: Bratislava Castle
blurb: Hilltop castle above the Danube with a Bratislava history museum and a baroque garden; the views are the main draw.

name: St. Martin's Cathedral
blurb: Gothic cathedral below the castle where Hungarian kings were crowned; entry is a cheap €2 and the interior is worth a look.

name: Museum of Transport
blurb: Historic cars, trams, bicycles, fire engines and model ships in the city's first railway station, close to the main station.
priceText: Adults €8; students and seniors 65–70 €4; children 3–6 and seniors 70+ €1; under 3 free; free first Wednesday of each month

name: Michael's Gate with Tower
blurb: 14th-century gate tower, 51 m tall with a green copper roof; one of the oldest landmarks in the old town.

name: KGB Krčma Gurmánov Bratislavy
blurb: Communism-themed pub with good beers at affordable prices in the city centre; a fun, late-running night out.

name: UFO
blurb: Bar, lounge and terrace in the saucer on top of the SNP Bridge, with Danube views; the restaurant is pricey.
priceText: Entrance €6.50, but free of charge if you eat in the restaurant

name: Slovak Pub
blurb: Traditional Slovak eatery on Obchodná serving halušky, the national dish of dumplings; reasonably priced, but portions run small.

name: Góvinda reštaurácia
blurb: Hare Krishna-run vegetarian and vegan canteen in the city centre; very affordable, but open on weekday lunch hours only.

name: Devín Castle
blurb: Ruined fortress on a rocky hill where the Morava meets the Danube, just outside the city; cheap in winter, with Roman roots.
priceText: €8 April to October, €6 November to March

name: Rijksmuseum
blurb: Dutch Golden Age masterpieces, including Rembrandt's Night Watch and Vermeer's Milkmaid; there is no student discount.

name: Van Gogh Museum
blurb: Largest collection of Van Gogh's paintings and drawings; tickets are online only and can sell out weeks ahead.

name: Anne Frank House
blurb: Secret annex where Anne Frank hid from the Nazis and wrote her diary; book online well ahead, as same-day slots are few.

name: Museum Willet-Holthuysen
blurb: Fully furnished 17th-century canal house with silverware, porcelain and books; a quiet, cheap alternative to the big museums.

name: Van der Linde
blurb: Bakery famous for Amsterdam's whipped ice cream, a creamy, melt-in-the-mouth treat; the almond cookies are good too.

name: Albina
blurb: Cheap, very good food in Zuid with plain surroundings; arrive before dinnertime or expect to wait for a table.

name: Sugar Factory
blurb: Art, music and theatre under one roof, with a nightclub at its heart; relaxed, eccentric and a bit different.

name: Hannekes Boom
blurb: Snug, unpolished bar on the IJ waterfront, good for a beer and a chat rather than a clubbing night.

name: ICE* Amsterdam
blurb: Open-air ice rink of about 1,400 m² on the Museumplein, open daily in winter; a fun skate beside the museums.

name: Brouwerij de Prael
blurb: Brewery, tasting room and beer shop in one, in the city centre; four beers for €10 is an easy way to sample local brews.
priceText: Brewery tour or beer tasting with four beers €10
when: Tasting room Tue–Sat 12:00–24:00, Sun 12:00–23:00; beer shop 12:00–19:00

name: Manneken Pis
blurb: Tiny bronze statue of a boy that is the city's cheeky symbol; free, open round the clock and often dressed up.

name: Royal Museums of Fine Arts of Belgium
blurb: Old Masters such as Bosch and Memling plus the Magritte Museum in one complex; major art at a fair price.
priceText: €8 adults per museum or €13 combo; €2.50 students/seniors/disabled; €1.25 children 12–18; under 12 free; free first Wednesday afternoon of the month

name: Musical Instruments Museum (MIM)
blurb: More than 7,000 instruments from around the world across four floors; an unusual and well-known collection.

name: Wiertz Museum
blurb: Former studio of the Romantic painter Antoine Wiertz, kept with its original atmosphere; quirky and free to visit.

name: Friterie Tabora
blurb: Locals' favourite frites stand with a huge range of sauces; open almost round the clock for a cheap bite.

name: Waffle Workshop
blurb: A 90-minute hands-on class to make Brussels waffles, with all ingredients and toppings and a take-home recipe.
priceText: General €28, student €25, kids €18, family €75 (2 adults & 2 kids)

name: Brussels Pub Crawl
blurb: Pub crawl with a free welcome beer, a mini beer tasting and drink discounts, visiting four bars or clubs in one evening.

name: Chez Moeder Lambic
blurb: Old-fashioned brown café with hundreds of obscure Belgian beers, many found nowhere else; a 25 cl beer costs €4.

name: Sandeman's Brussels Free Tours
blurb: Informative three-hour walking tour of the centre on a pay-what-you-wish basis; groups can be large, so arrive early.

name: Nemo 33
blurb: Diving pool 34.5 m deep, filled with non-chlorinated spring water; a unique swim, dive or photo stop.

name: British Museum
blurb: Vast world collection from Egyptian mummies to the Rosetta Stone; permanent galleries are free, though some items are contested.

name: Tower of London
blurb: Royal fortress founded in 1066 and home of the Crown Jewels; pricey, but one of the city's essential sights.

name: St Paul's Cathedral
blurb: Christopher Wren's domed cathedral (1675–1710), rebuilt after the Great Fire; climb to the dome for big views over the City.
priceText: Adult £27 (Mon–Sat sightseeing); discounts for families, groups and concessions (no amounts given)

name: Bank of England Museum
blurb: Free museum on the Bank's history since 1694, where you can lift a real gold bar; photos allowed, but no flash.

name: Lower Marsh Street street food
blurb: Street-food stalls on Lower Marsh with Korean, Cuban, Peruvian, Nigerian and Ethiopian dishes; a varied, quick lunch.

name: Pembroke Lodge
blurb: Self-service restaurant in Richmond Park with good-value British food and a lovely terrace view for lunch or afternoon tea.

name: Fabric
blurb: Cathedral-sized underground club with big dance acts and long queues at peak times; NUS card holders get a discount.

name: Fitzroy Tavern
blurb: Samuel Smith's pub in Fitzrovia with good, cheap beer and a classic boozer atmosphere; an easy budget first stop.

name: Somerset House Ice Rink
blurb: Ice rink in the Somerset House courtyard, a Londoner favourite; go in the evening when the Christmas tree is lit.
priceText: Most London rinks £10–12 (adults) for an hour, including skate hire

name: Dennis Severs' House
blurb: Candlelit 18th-century Huguenot townhouse with rooms staged as if the family just left; atmospheric and unlike any museum.
when: Sun 12:00–16:00; Mon 12:00–14:00; silent nights Mon & Wed 17:00–21:00

name: Edinburgh Castle
blurb: Fortress on volcanic rock, in use for about 1,100 years and still the army's Scottish headquarters; book online to save.
priceText: Adult (16–64) £23.50 online, £26.00 walk-up; concession (65+, unemployed) £19.00 online, £21.00 walk-up; concessions do not cover students

name: National Museum of Scotland
blurb: Scotland's national museum in a lofty Victorian hall, covering Scottish and world history, science and design; free entry.

name: Scottish National Gallery
blurb: Scotland's fine art from the Renaissance to the 20th century; the permanent displays are free, big shows cost extra.
priceText: Free, charges for major temporary exhibitions

name: Writers' Museum
blurb: Tall 1622 house celebrating Burns, Scott and Stevenson; a suggested £3 donation buys a cosy trip through Scottish literature.

name: The Original Mosque Kitchen
blurb: Inexpensive chicken and vegetable curries that have fed generations of Edinburgh students; big portions for the price.

name: Tempting Tattie
blurb: Inexpensive takeaway for hot traditional baked potatoes; a warm, cheap lunch or snack, mostly to take away.

name: The Oxford Bar
blurb: Classic Scottish pub that features in Ian Rankin's Rebus novels; cosy, unpretentious and good for a first pint.

name: Whiski
blurb: Touristy but fun: Scottish food, live music nightly from 9:30pm and hundreds of whiskies; sit near the front for the music.

name: Scotch Whisky Experience
blurb: Guided tour of how whisky is made, with a vast bottle collection; the Silver tour suits beginners.

name: Murrayfield Ice Rink
blurb: Popular ice rink with leisure sessions and Fri/Sat night ice-discos; home rink of the Edinburgh Capitals ice hockey team.
when: Leisure sessions; ice-discos Fri and Sat nights

name: Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum
blurb: Red-sandstone Victorian art and natural history museum with a huge free collection and a hanging Spitfire; great on a rainy day.

name: Glasgow Cathedral
blurb: Medieval Gothic cathedral of St Mungo, Glasgow's patron saint, with his tomb in the crypt; largely intact since the Reformation.

name: Willow Tea Rooms
blurb: Tea rooms designed by Charles Rennie Mackintosh for temperance campaigner Kate Cranston; a guided tour explains the design.

name: Fossil Grove
blurb: Fossilised forest of giant prehistoric trees, about 330 million years old, found during quarrying; free to see at weekends.

name: Guido's Coronation Restaurant
blurb: Glasgow institution by the Barrowlands, praised for healthy portions and competitively priced food; a solid lunch stop.

name: Paesano Pizza
blurb: Neapolitan wood-fired pizza in a big industrial-chic room, with branches on Great Western Road and Pollokshaws Road.

name: Nice'N'Sleazy
blurb: Student favourite mixing a bar and nightclub, with live bands most nights downstairs and small acts upstairs; over-18s only.

name: Horseshoe Bar
blurb: Traditional pub with one of Europe's longest continuous bars and good pub food; a lively old-school night out.

name: City Chambers tour
blurb: Free guided tour of the 1888 Italian Renaissance council headquarters: marble staircases, lobbies and the debating chamber.

name: Wellpark Brewery tour (Tennent's)
blurb: Tennent's brewery tours; the family has brewed on the site since 1556, making Tennent's Lager, the brand's best-seller.

name: Science and Industry Museum
blurb: Industrial-heritage museum on the site of the world's first passenger railway, with working cotton looms; mostly free.
priceText: Free, except for temporary exhibits (prices vary)

name: Manchester Art Gallery
blurb: Huge collection of 19th-century and older paintings in a Sir Charles Barry building; free entry, closed at Christmas and New Year.

name: John Rylands Library
blurb: Stunning Gothic library, now open to all floors and free to enter, with a new café on the Spinningfields side.

name: St. Mary's (The Hidden Gem)
blurb: Oldest purpose-built post-Reformation Catholic church in England (1794), tucked away in the city centre; active, quiet and free.

name: Mackie Mayor
blurb: Food hall in a Grade II-listed 1858 market building with six independent kitchens and bars; shared tables and local beer.

name: Wing's Dai Pai Dong
blurb: Cantonese, Thai and Japanese dishes around a sushi counter; the Hong Kong-style roast dishes are good value and well made.

name: Matt and Phreds
blurb: Tucked-away jazz club with bands nightly except Monday; free entry before 8pm, and seats must be booked to sit.
when: Open until 02:00 most nights; jazz from 22:00 (not Mon)

name: Sofa
blurb: Relaxed bar with sofas and wooden floors, DJs at weekends and tickets for big club nights; pints are cheap.

name: Manchester City stadium tour and museum
blurb: Stadium tour and club museum at the Etihad, home of Manchester City; a good-value option for football fans.
priceText: Museum and stadium tour: adults £7, concessions £4.50

name: Chill Factore (The Snow Centre)
blurb: 180 m artificial-snow slope for skiing and snowboarding in The Quays area; lift passes sold by the hour, month or year.
